issue.title: sase bead doctor reports 14 settled historical event-stream rewrites as permanent ERRORs
issue.description:
Discovered 2026-08-16 after repairing the bead-store wedge.

'sase bead doctor' on a healthy, fully-synced store prints 14 ERROR lines for event-stream rewrites that are already settled history, e.g.:

  ERROR: bead event stream sase-m5 rewrote event 3; first offending commit a2c29f164c6a
  ERROR: bead event stream sase-j7 is shorter than its own history: missing events 62-63 present in ancestor 7e3d27461b3a
  ERROR: bead event stream sase-mk rewrote event 2; first offending commit 4dfa41f5ad5d

These are backward-looking. The guard already settled each one at the time by restoring ancestor bytes, and the store commits and pushes cleanly now: verified by three real mutations (close sase-m9.3.1.5, close sase-mi.6, and the 8-agent epic graph commit for sase-mq) all committing and pushing without incident, and by mutating one bead in a full 853-stream scratch copy and confirming every other stream stayed byte-identical.

The problem is signal quality, not correctness. A doctor that always prints 14 ERRORs on a healthy store trains agents and the owner to ignore its ERROR section, so a genuinely new rewrite will not stand out. That directly cost time during this incident: distinguishing the one live, blocking rewrite from the 14 dead ones required manual event-by-event comparison.

Scope: give settled historical rewrites a distinct, non-ERROR classification (baseline/acknowledged/settled) so ERROR is reserved for rewrites that are currently blocking, and keep the historical set inspectable on demand. Deliberately excludes any history rewrite of the bead store; the committed events stay as they are.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-li — that task explains at least one of the 14 (the sase-j7 'shorter than its own history: missing events 62-63' entry is exactly its concurrent-sync deletion defect); classifying the historical set should not hide a recurrence of it.
RELATED: sase-mr — the same incident's other follow-up; per-stream writes would shrink how often a single bad event can produce store-wide rewrite reports.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction by land agent sase-mq.8.land during parent sase-mq readiness checks on master d10fe53024144a0084501c349642552cccc8e033: sase bead doctor reports eight historical stream-integrity ERRORs (sase-j7 shorter than history; sase-m7, sase-lk, sase-me, sase-mh, sase-jw, sase-mk, and sase-ml rewrote events) even though the current sase-mq graph and linked plans are healthy and 336 ownership regressions pass. This matches the existing signal-quality defect: settled historical findings remain permanent ERROR output and obscure current blockers. No new task created.

payload.entry: TRIAGE 2026-08-16 (workspace sase_13, master 630f4ea71). 'sase bead doctor' against the live store now prints ZERO 'rewrote event' / 'shorter than its own history' ERROR lines; the only output is pre-existing WARNING/NOTE lines (beads.db missing, 14 malformed design refs, 14 design-ref owner mismatches, 3 artifact-ref warnings, 454 redundant close events). Root cause of the disappearance: diagnose_event_stream_history (src/sase/bead/_stream_integrity.py:235) sources its records from stream_history_records (src/sase/bead/_stream_integrity_git.py:145), which passes --max-count=_HISTORY_COMMIT_LIMIT to git log over the stream dir. Settled rewrites therefore scroll out of the window on their own as the store commits, which is exactly the self-limiting behavior this bead asked to be engineered. All 14 named streams (sase-m5, sase-j7, sase-mk, sase-m7, sase-lk, sase-me, sase-mh, sase-jw, sase-ml) are gone from the output. Refile with a +1 if a rewrite finding ever persists across the window while the store is otherwise healthy. The related concerns remain tracked: sase-li (concurrent-sync deletion) is closed, sase-mr (per-stream writes) stays open.

payload.close_reason: Premise falsified: the historical rewrite findings are not permanent -- they age out of the doctor's bounded commit window, and the store reports zero today.
